newsitem.title: UK: Currency concerns pressure Brady prices.
newsitem.headline: Currency concerns pressure Brady prices.

text.p: Brady bonds are expected to come under pressure this week amid continued currency concerns and nervousness ahead of testimony by the U.S. Federal Reserve chief on Tuesday, traders said on Monday.

"We were hoping we might start with a nice quiet week but if you look at the Asian currencies, they have been under pressure so the focus (on currencies) will be in peoples minds," said one emerging market trader at a U.S. Investment bank in London.
Growing concerns about Brazil's current account deficit and any spillover effect from the Asian currency markets could further pressure the country's Brady bonds, traders added.
"In particular, people will be looking at the Brazilian stock market and any reaction in the currencies," said one trader.

"I think it is fairly easy to call the fact that speculators are going to hunt around the world looking for countries with current account deficits," said another trader at a major U.S. bank in London.
Brazilian Brady's, which suffered steep losses on Friday following a sharp selloff in the country's stock market, were marginally weaker on Monday.
The country's "C" bonds were 1/2 lower at 80-7/8 bid and its par bonds were 1/4 softer at 69-3/4 bid.
Meanwhile, market experts said investors will focus on comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to the House Banking Subcommittee on Tuesday.

"Humphrey Hawkins is not traditionally a market friendly commentary so we have that and we have the local markets so if both of those end up as negatives than the Brady market will have a very bad week," the first trader said.
Among Eastern European Brady instruments, Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1/4 lower at 74 bid and Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were unchanged at 92 bid.
